strategies.title: Single Candidate
strategies.description: When a cell can only contain one possible number because all other numbers are already present in its row, column, or 3x3 box.
examples: Imagine a row with numbers 1-8 already present - the empty cell must be 9

strategies.title: Single Position
strategies.description: When a number can only go in one specific cell within a row, column, or box because all other positions are already occupied.
examples: If a 3x3 box has numbers 1-8 except for 9, and only one cell is empty, that cell must be 9

strategies.title: Row/Column Check
strategies.description: Eliminate candidates by checking which numbers are already present in the row and column.
examples: If a cell's row has 1,2,3 and column has 4,5, the possible numbers are 6-9

strategies.title: Box Line Reduction
strategies.description: When all possible positions for a number in a box are in one row/column, eliminate that number from the rest of the row/column outside the box.
examples: If in a box, number 5 can only go in the middle row, remove 5 from that row in other boxes

strategies.title: Obvious Pairs
strategies.description: When two cells in a unit have the same two candidates, those numbers can be eliminated from other cells in the unit.
examples: If two cells in a column can only be 2 or 3, remove 2 and 3 from other cells in that column

strategies.title: Pointing Pairs
strategies.description: When two possible positions for a number in a box align in a row/column, eliminate that number from the rest of the row/column.
examples: If in a box, 7 can only go in two cells in the same column, remove 7 from that column in other boxes

strategies.title: Last Remaining Cell
strategies.description: When all but one number have been placed in a row, column, or box, the last remaining number must go in the empty cell.
examples: If a row has numbers 1-8 with one empty cell, that cell must be 9

strategies.title: Candidate Highlighting
strategies.description: Systematically eliminate impossible candidates by visually marking possible numbers in empty cells.
examples: Mark all possible numbers for a cell based on its row, column, and box
When only one number remains unmarked, it must be the solution

strategies.title: Cross-Hatching
strategies.description: Methodically scan each box while checking against its row and column constraints.
examples: Focus on one box at a time, checking which numbers are missing
For each missing number, check rows/columns to find possible positions

strategies.title: Candidate Lines
strategies.description: When a number's possible positions within a block are all in the same row or column, eliminating it from that row/column in other blocks.
examples: If in a 3x3 box, 5 can only be in the top row, remove 5 from the rest of that row in other boxes

strategies.title: Naked Pairs
strategies.description: When two cells in a unit contain the exact same two possible numbers, eliminating those numbers from other cells in the unit.
examples: If two cells in a row can only be 3 or 7, remove 3 and 7 from other cells in that row

strategies.title: Naked Triples
strategies.description: When three cells in a unit contain only the same three possible numbers, eliminating those numbers from other cells in the unit.
examples: If three cells in a column can only be 4,5,6 in some combination, remove these numbers from other cells in the column

strategies.title: Hidden Triples
strategies.description: When three numbers appear only in three cells of a unit, eliminating other candidates from those cells.
examples: If numbers 2,4,6 appear only in three cells of a box, those cells must contain these numbers

strategies.title: X-Wing (Basic)
strategies.description: When a number appears in exactly two rows and two columns forming a rectangle, eliminating it from those rows/columns outside the rectangle.
examples: If 7 appears only in rows 2 and 5 at columns 3 and 7, remove other 7s in those columns

strategies.title: Simple Coloring
strategies.description: Using two colors to track possibilities for a number to find contradictions or certain placements.
examples: If all possible 5s are connected in a chain where colors alternate, you can eliminate possibilities that would force two 5s in the same unit

strategies.title: Y-Wing
strategies.description: A technique using three cells connected like a pivot and two pincers to eliminate candidates.
examples: If cell A (3,5) connects to B (3,7) and C (5,7), any cell seeing both B and C cannot be 7

strategies.title: Skyscraper
strategies.description: Two strong links for a candidate that share a common row or column, allowing eliminations.
examples: If candidate 5 appears twice in a column and forms a 'skyscraper' shape with another column
Can eliminate 5s from cells visible to both 'towers' of the skyscraper

strategies.title: Two-String Kite
strategies.description: A number that connects a row and column through a shared box, creating elimination opportunities.
examples: When a candidate in a row connects to a candidate in a column via a shared box
Eliminate the candidate from the intersection cell

strategies.title: Hidden Pairs
strategies.description: When two numbers only appear in the same two cells of a unit, eliminating other candidates from those cells.
examples: If in a column, numbers 4 and 5 only appear in two cells together, those cells must contain 4 and 5

strategies.title: X-Wing
strategies.description: When a number appears in exactly two rows and two columns forming a rectangle, eliminating it from those rows/columns outside the rectangle.
examples: If 7 appears only in rows 2 and 5 at columns 3 and 7, remove other 7s in those columns

strategies.title: Swordfish
strategies.description: An advanced version of X-Wing using three rows and columns instead of two.
examples: If number 3 appears in three rows and exactly three columns, aligned in a specific pattern, you can eliminate other 3s in those columns

strategies.title: XYZ-Wing
strategies.description: An extension of Y-Wing using three cells where the pivot contains three candidates.
examples: If cell A (4,5,6) connects to B (4,7) and C (5,7), any cell seeing all three cannot be 7

strategies.title: W-Wing
strategies.description: A technique using two cells with the same two candidates connected through a strong link.
examples: If two cells (1,9) are connected through a chain of 1s, one of them must be 9

strategies.title: Jellyfish
strategies.description: An advanced pattern similar to Swordfish but using four rows and columns.
examples: When a number appears in four rows and exactly four columns in a specific alignment, allowing eliminations

strategies.title: Unique Rectangle
strategies.description: A pattern that prevents multiple solutions by forcing certain placements.
examples: If four cells form a rectangle with the same two candidates, additional constraints must apply to prevent multiple solutions

strategies.title: XY-Chain
strategies.description: A chain of connected cells where each link shares a candidate with the next, allowing endpoint eliminations.
examples: 4-6 → 6-9 → 9-2 → 2-7 chain means either end must be 4 or 7
Eliminate candidates visible to both ends of the chain

strategies.title: ALS-XZ
strategies.description: Two Almost Locked Sets that share restricted candidates, enabling advanced eliminations.
examples: When two groups of cells share exactly one candidate
That shared candidate can be eliminated from visible cells

strategies.title: Death Blossom
strategies.description: An advanced pattern using a stem cell connected to multiple ALS petals.
examples: A central cell connected to three ALS groups
Eliminations occur based on shared constraints

strategies.title: Digit Forcing Chain
strategies.description: Tests candidate placements to find contradictions or verifications across multiple cells.
examples: Assume a candidate is true and follow implications
If it leads to contradiction, the candidate must be false

strategies.title: Multi-Coloring
strategies.description: Extended coloring with multiple colors to track complex candidate interactions.
examples: Using 4+ colors to track candidate dependencies
Find eliminations where colors conflict

strategies.title: Pattern Overlay
strategies.description: Superimposes candidate patterns to identify unavoidable eliminations.
examples: Map all possible positions for a candidate
Find cells where the candidate must be eliminated
